mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC stabilized at roughly -28 to -29 over the last two weeks after a deep trough at t-2w, indicating the shock has passed and mobility is reverting toward its pre-trough level. This stabilizing momentum should continue, producing a modestly higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -39.9 at t-2w to -28.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite two consecutive weeks of stabilization near -28 to -29.

mechanism_narrative: The decision point falls in mid-December, immediately preceding the Christmas and New Year holiday shopping window. Historically this period drives a seasonal surge in retail and recreation visits regardless of the preceding weekly trend, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-12-15, immediately preceding the Christmas and New Year holiday period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks spanning the Christmas/New Year period relative to the prior two weeks despite no new mobility restriction being announced.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has already fallen sharply (from -26.7 to -36.6 at t-2w) before partially recovering. If TRANSIT resumes a decline of more than 10 points week-on-week, this signals renewed public caution or new restrictions that will suppress discretionary retail and recreation visits over the following weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week from its current -27.1 level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -26.7 to -36.6 between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise or stay flat even after TRANSIT drops by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT move together as joint indicators of overall out-of-home economic activity. When both decline simultaneously, it reflects either renewed restrictions or voluntary withdrawal from public life, which jointly depresses retail and recreation visits beyond what either series alone would predict; when both are stable or rising together, RETAIL_REC should rise.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall simultaneously by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -35.6 to -46.0 and TRANSIT fell from -26.7 to -36.6 in the same week (t-2w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline jointly by more than 5 points in a given week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has risen unusually for mid-December, from -5.7 to +3.7 over three weeks, which is atypical for winter in Lombardy. This suggests households are substituting outdoor, lower-density activities for indoor retail and recreation venues, likely due to lingering infection caution, which should pull RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -5.7 at t-3w to +3.7 at t-0w despite winter season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with continued PARKS increases rather than falling, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained persistently elevated near +9 to +10 for the last three weeks, indicating sustained time spent at home consistent with ongoing restrictive policy or voluntary compliance measures. This persistent elevation should continue to suppress RETAIL_REC below its recent trailing average over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held between +7.9 and +9.7 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even as RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +9.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility leads RETAIL_REC because essential shopping trips often co-occur with or precede discretionary retail visits in the same shopping trips. GROCERY_PHARM has recovered from -21.9 to -10.0 over the last two weeks, and this recovery should transmit to RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -21.9 at t-2w to -10.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a continued GROCERY_PHARM recovery above -10.

mechanism_narrative: In December 2021, Lombardy faces an emerging Omicron wave; even absent formal lockdowns, rising case counts typically trigger voluntary avoidance of crowded indoor retail and recreation venues. Under this pandemic-wave regime, the prior stabilization of RETAIL_REC will reverse into decline over the next four weeks as caution increases ahead of holiday gatherings.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-12-15 coincides with emerging Omicron wave in Italy
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise or stabilize through the holiday period despite rising regional case counts and no formal new restriction.
